Between 1990 and 1993 Europe gained a dozen new countries, all in red on this map. Here is how each wave happened, from one map of states born after the Iron Curtain fell.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Germany is the gold one. East Germany's parliament voted on 23 August 1990 to join the Federal Republic, and unification took effect on 3 October 1990. Five eastern states joined and Berlin became one city-state.

2/ Lithuania is marked 1990. On 11 March 1990 its parliament proclaimed the re-establishment of the Lithuanian state, the first Soviet republic to declare independence. Estonia and Latvia are marked 1991.
3/ The Soviet Union formally ceased to exist on 26 December 1991. All 15 union republics became independent; on this map that means Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Belarus, Ukraine and Moldova.
4/ Yugoslavia broke up in stages. Slovenia and Croatia declared independence on 25 June 1991, North Macedonia on 25 September 1991, and Bosnia and Herzegovina on 3 March 1992.
5/ Czechoslovakia ended by a Federal Assembly vote on 25 November 1992. It split into the Czech Republic and Slovakia on 1 January 1993, so both carry 1993 on the map.
Count the red: 12 new countries on this map, plus a reunified Germany, in just four years. Follow @forummapping for more maps. Borders: CShapes 2.0 (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
